```{r}
# seaparate out controls from samples
physeq_mse1.controls <- subset_samples(physeq_rare, Stress_ID %in% c("Negative_Control")) %>% prune_taxa(taxa_sums(.)>0,.)

#remove controls: 
physeq_mse1.filtered1 <- subset_samples(physeq_rare, !(Stress_ID %in% c("Negative_Control")))

#remove sample ID 47 for low reads: 
physeq_mse1.filtered2 <- subset_samples(physeq_mse1.filtered1, !(ID %in% c("47")))

# remove sample ID 164 (extreme outlier)
physeq_mse1.filtered3 <- subset_samples(physeq_mse1.filtered2, !(ID %in% c("164")))
```

```{r}
# Calculate alpha diversity and add to data frame:
alphadiv <- estimate_richness(physeq_mse1.filtered3, measures=c('Observed', 'Chao1','Shannon', 'InvSimpson')) %>%
  as.data.frame() 
# Convert to true diversity https://twitter.com/derekseveri/status/1106359475756240898?lang=en
alphadiv$Shannon_true_diversity <- exp(alphadiv$Shannon)
rownames(alphadiv) <- str_replace_all(rownames(alphadiv),'\\.','-') # change row names . to - for compatibility with phyloseq

rownames(alphadiv) <- sample_names(physeq_mse1.filtered3)

smd <- cbind(sample_data(physeq_mse1.filtered3), alphadiv)

sample_data(physeq_mse1.filtered3) <- smd  # update in phyloseq object

# save 
save(physeq_mse1.filtered3, file="~/Desktop/FDA_Lab/Experiment1/MicrobiomeProcessing4/phyloseq_filtered_alphadiv_updated.Rdata")
```

```{r}
# multiplicative model on alpha diversity 
analyze_all_combos <- function(smd) {
  
  # extract all treatment summaries
  treatment_summaries <- smd %>% 
    group_by(Stress_ID) %>% 
    summarize( 
      mean_shannon = mean(Shannon, na.rm = TRUE), 
      sd_shannon = sd(Shannon, na.rm = TRUE), 
      n = n(), 
      .groups = "drop")
  # define all combinations to test 
  combinations <- list(
    #pairwise 
    list(singles = c("MP", "Drought"), combo = "Drought_MP"), 
    list(singles = c("MP", "Herbicide"), combo = "Herbicide_MP"), 
    list(singles = c("MP", "Antibiotic"), combo = "Antibiotic_MP"), 
    list(singles = c("Drought", "Herbicide"), combo = "Drought_Herbicide"),
    list(singles = c("Drought", "Antibiotic"), combo = "Antibiotic_Drought"),
    list(singles = c("Herbicide", "Antibiotic"), combo = "Antibiotic_Herbicide"),
    #three-way 
    list(singles = c("MP", "Drought", "Herbicide"), combo = "Drought_Herbicide_MP"), 
    list(singles = c("MP", "Drought", "Antibiotic"), combo = "Antibiotic_Drought_MP"), 
    list(singles = c("MP", "Herbicide", "Antibiotic"), combo = "Antibiotic_Herbicide_MP"), 
    list(singles = c("Drought", "Herbicide", "Antibiotic"), combo = "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide"),
    #four-way 
    list(singles = c("MP", "Drought", "Herbicide", "Antibiotic"), combo = "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide_MP")
  )
  calculate_effect_size <- function(combo_info, summaries) {
    control <- summaries %>% filter(Stress_ID == "Control")
    combo_data <- summaries %>% filter(Stress_ID == combo_info$combo)
    
    if(nrow(control) == 0 | nrow(combo_data) == 0) return(NULL)
    
    # get single stressor data 
    single_data <- map_dfr(combo_info$singles, ~{
      summaries %>% filter(Stress_ID == .x)
    })
    
    if(nrow(single_data) == 0) return(NULL)
    
    # multiplicative expectation 
    single_means <- single_data$mean_shannon
    Xc <-  control$mean_shannon
    X_obs <- combo_data$mean_shannon
    
    X_exp <- prod(single_means) / Xc^(length(single_means) -1)
    
    # simple effect size 
    ES <- log(X_obs) - log(X_exp)
    
    # VARIANCE using delta method (all treatments contribute)
  k <- length(single_means)  # number of single stressors
  
  var_ES <- (
    combo_data$sd_shannon^2 / (combo_data$n * X_obs^2) +           # Observed combo
    sum(single_data$sd_shannon^2 / (single_data$n * single_data$mean_shannon^2)) +  # Singles
    (k - 1) * (control$sd_shannon^2 / (control$n * Xc^2))          # Control (raised to k-1)
  )
  
  SE <- sqrt(var_ES)
  CI_lower <- ES - 1.96 * SE
  CI_upper <- ES + 1.96 * SE
  
  # Classification
  classification <- case_when(
    CI_lower > 0 ~ "Synergistic",
    CI_upper < 0 ~ "Antagonistic",
    CI_lower <= 0 & CI_upper >= 0 ~ "Null",
    TRUE ~ "Reversal"
  )
  
    data.frame(
      combination = combo_info$combo,
      singles_used = paste(combo_info$singles, collapse = "_"), 
      observed = X_obs, 
      expected = X_exp, 
      effect_size = ES, 
      SE = SE, 
      CI_lower = CI_lower, 
      CI_upper = CI_upper,
      classification = classification,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }
  
  # apply to all combos 
  results <- map_dfr(combinations, ~calculate_effect_size(.x, treatment_summaries))
  return(results)
} 

# run it 
results <- analyze_all_combos(smd)
print(results)

plot_data <- results %>%
  mutate(n_stressors = str_count(singles_used, "_") + 2)

shannondiv_multi_effects <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = reorder(combination, n_stressors), y = effect_size, color = classification)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "black", size = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = CI_lower, ymax = CI_upper), width = 0.2, alpha = 0.9) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Antagonistic" = "#4363d8", "Synergistic" = "#e6194B", 
                               "Null" = "gray50", "Reversal" = "purple")) +
  labs(x = "Stressor Combinations", y = "Effect Size (95% CI)",
       title = "Shannon's Diversity",
       color = "Interaction Type")

ggsave("~/Desktop/FDA_Lab/Experiment1/plots/shannon_multiplicative_effect_sizes.svg", shannondiv_multi_effects)
```

```{r} 
# relative abundance (by Family) - only showing top 15 Families since there are so many 
ps_family <- tax_glom(physeq_mse1.filtered3, taxrank = "Family", NArm = TRUE)

top_families <- df_family %>% 
  group_by(Family) %>% 
  summarize(mean_abund = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(mean_abund)) %>% 
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
```

## Ordination 
```{r}
RDA.bray.mse1 <- ordinate(physeq_mse1.filtered3, method='RDA',distance='bray',formula=~Stress_ID)
#Color by Stress ID 
RDA_16S_bray <- plot_ordination(physeq_mse1.filtered3, RDA.bray.mse1)
RDA_16S_bray[["layers"]][[1]][["geom"]][["default_aes"]][["colour"]] <- 'white'
RDA_16S_bray <- RDA_16S_bray + 
  geom_point(aes(color = Stress_ID), size = 3, alpha = 0.90) +
  theme(legend.text.align = 0) + 
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
        "Control" = "#e6194B",
        "MP" = "#3cb44b",
        "Drought" = "#ffe119",
        "Herbicide" = "#4363d8",
        "Antibiotic" = "#f58231",
        "Drought_MP" = "#42d4f4",
        "Antibiotic_MP" = "#f032e6",
        "Herbicide_MP" = "#469990",
        "Antibiotic_Herbicide" = "#9A6324",
        "Drought_Herbicide" = "#800000",
        "Antibiotic_Drought" = "#911eb4",
        "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide" = "#bfef45", 
        "Antibiotic_Drought_MP" = "#808000",
        "Antibiotic_Herbicide_MP" = "#000075",
        "Drought_Herbicide_MP" = "#a9a9a9", 
        "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide_MP" = "#000000"
    ))
ggsave("~/Desktop/FDA_Lab/Experiment1/plots/RDA_bray_ordination.svg", RDA_16S_bray)


# Permuation test
# testing overall RDA significance 
permutest(RDA.bray.mse1)
# trying to find R^2... 
R2_constrained_bray <- sum(RDA.bray.mse1$CCA$eig) / sum(RDA.bray.mse1$tot.chi)
print(paste("R2 = ", round(R2_constrained_bray, 3),
            "(", round(R2_constrained_bray*100, 1), "% explained)")) # Stress_ID explains 30.5% of total variation in bacterial communities. This is a strong result for microbial ecology 

# Trying unconstrained ordination (PCoA). Unconstrained ordinations use only the ASV matrix (or distance matrix); environmental variables are not part of the algorithm. The axes represent the main gradients of variation in community composition, whatever their causes (measured or unmeasured)
pcoa_ord <- ordinate(physeq_mse1.filtered3, method = "PCoA", distance = "bray")

unconstrained_ordination <- plot_ordination(physeq_mse1.filtered3, pcoa_ord, type = "samples", color = "Stress_ID") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_bw() + 
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
        "Control" = "#e6194B",
        "MP" = "#3cb44b",
```

Variance partitioning 
```{r}
# variance partitioning - 2 options: 
  # 1: permanova 
  # 2: dbRDA multivariate ranking 
# trying both!

# 1: PERMANOVA 
dist_full <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_mse1.filtered3, method = "bray") 
dist_full_mat <- as.matrix(dist_full)

env_vars <- c("Stress_ID", "Depth.mm", "Average.Diameter.mm", "Number.of.Root.Tips", "Total.Root.Length.mm", "Shoot_Biomass", "Root_Biomass", 
                                             "Maximum.Number.of.Roots", "Maximum.Width.mm", "Width.to.Depth.Ratio", "Convex.Area.mm2", "Maximum.Diameter.mm", 
                                             "Volume.mm3", "Average.Root.Orientation.deg", "Medium.Angle.Frequency")

# test each variable individually 
r2_values <- sapply(env_vars, function(var) {
  adonis2(dist_full_mat ~ smd[[var]], permuatations = 999)$R2[1]
})

# rank by R2 (variation explained)
rank_env <- data.frame(
  Variable = env_vars, 
  R2 = r2_values, 
  P_value = sapply(env_vars, function(var) {
    adonis2(dist_full_mat ~ smd[[var]], permutations = 999)$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  })
) %>% arrange(desc(R2)) 

rank_env #R2 = % variation each variable explains :D 

# rank for plotting
rank_env <- rank_env %>% 
  arrange(desc(R2)) %>% 
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = Variable), 
         R2_pct = R2 * 100) # convert to percentage for plotting 

variance_part <- ggplot(rank_env, aes(x = R2_pct, y = Variable)) + 
  geom_col() +  
  labs(x = "Variance Explained (%)")

ggsave("~/Desktop/FDA_Lab/Experiment1/plots/variance_part.svg", variance_part)

## take stress ID out of the model... 
env_vars_no_stress <- c("Depth.mm", "Average.Diameter.mm", "Number.of.Root.Tips", "Total.Root.Length.mm", "Shoot_Biomass", "Root_Biomass", 
                                             "Maximum.Number.of.Roots", "Maximum.Width.mm", "Width.to.Depth.Ratio", "Convex.Area.mm2", "Maximum.Diameter.mm", 
                                             "Volume.mm3", "Average.Root.Orientation.deg", "Medium.Angle.Frequency")
r2_values2 <- sapply(env_vars_no_stress, function(var) {
  adonis2(dist_full_mat ~ smd[[var]], permuatations = 999)$R2[1]
})

# rank by R2 (variation explained)
rank_env2 <- data.frame(
  Variable = env_vars_no_stress, 
  R2 = r2_values2, 
  P_value = sapply(env_vars_no_stress, function(var) {
    adonis2(dist_full_mat ~ smd[[var]], permutations = 999)$`Pr(>F)`[1]
  })
) %>% arrange(desc(R2)) 

rank_env2

# ok... now I want to try adding my single stressors to see if that works 
adonis2(dist_full_mat ~ Stress_ID, data = smd, permutations = 999)
## this shows a single R2 output indicating the % microbiome variation explained by all stressors combined 

# to rank individual stressors: 
stress_levels <- unique(smd$Stress_ID)[unique(smd$Stress_ID) != "Control"]

r2_stressors <- sapply(stress_levels, function(trt) {
  # Compare this treatment vs everything else
  smd$trt_binary <- ifelse(smd$Stress_ID == trt, 1, 0)
  adonis2(dist_full_mat ~ trt_binary, data = smd, permutations = 999)$R2[1]
})

data.frame(Stressor = stress_levels, R2 = r2_stressors) %>% arrange(desc(R2)) # gives R2 for each stress treatment 



# 2: dbRDA multivariate ranking 

# fit model with all variables 
fit <- capscale(dist_full_mat ~ Stress_ID + (Depth.mm + Root_Biomass + Shoot_Biomass + 
                                               Total.Root.Length.mm + Average.Diameter.mm + Surface.Area.mm2 +
                                               Number.of.Root.Tips) ^ 2, # main + all pairwise interactions among these 7
                data = smd,
                dist = "bray")

# overall model R²
rda_r2 <- RsquareAdj(fit)$r.squared
print(paste("Total R² =", round(rda_r2, 3)))

# individual variable importance (P-VALUES)
anova_terms <- anova(fit, by = "terms", permutations = 999)
print(anova_terms)
```

# Building a 16x16 treatment-by-treatment Bray-Curtis matrix, where each cell is the mean Bray-Curtis distance between all replicates in replicates in treatment A and all replicates in treatment B (between-group mean pair distances)
```{r}
# bray-curtis distance between all samples 
dist_bc <- as.matrix(phyloseq::distance(physeq_mse1.filtered3, method = "bray"))

# get treatment labels (16 levels)
Stress <- smd$Stress_ID

# compute mean pairwise distance between each pair of treatments 
ntreats <- length(unique(Stress))
dist_mean_treat <- matrix(NA, nrow = ntreats, ncol = ntreats)
rownames(dist_mean_treat) <- colnames(dist_mean_treat) <- sort(unique(Stress))

# Convert Stress to factor to guarantee levels are 1–16
Stress <- as.factor(Stress)

# Loop over treatment pairs
for (t1 in levels(Stress)) {
  s1 <- which(Stress == t1)  # sample indices in treatment t1
  for (t2 in levels(Stress)) {
    s2 <- which(Stress == t2)  # sample indices in treatment t2
    
    # All cross‑pair distances: every rep in t1 vs every rep in t2
    d_cross <- dist_bc[s1, s2]
    
    # Mean distance (t1 vs t2)
    dist_mean_treat[t1, t2] <- mean(d_cross)
  }
}

# now dist_mean_treat should be a 16x16 matrix
dist_mean_treat
# note that the distance between 1:1 comparisons (like Control vs Control) are not 0 because the mean pair distance represents the average dissimilarity among the replicates in that treatment. This essentially reflects the within-group spread or variation.
# remember that bray-curtis is dissimilarity so distances closer to 0 are identical while distances closer 1 are completely dissimilar 

# creating a plot with the distances from each treatment to the control: 
control_label <- "Control"

# extract distance from Control to all other treatments 
treats <-  rownames(dist_mean_treat)

# drop control from x-axis 
other_treats <- treats[treats !=control_label]

# mean distance from control to each other treatment 
d_control_to_others <- dist_mean_treat[control_label, other_treats]

# put into a data frame for ggplot 
df_plot <- data.frame(
  Treatment = other_treats, 
  Distance_to_Control = d_control_to_others
) 

# sort df_plot by treatment so the x-axis is in a specific order: 
treatment_order <- factor(c("MP", "Drought", "Herbicide", "Antibiotic",
                          "Drought_MP", "Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_MP", 
                          "Drought_Herbicide", "Antibiotic_Drought", "Antibiotic_Herbicide",
                          "Drought_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_MP", 
                          "Antibiotic_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide", 
                          "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide_MP"), 
                         levels = c("MP", "Drought", "Herbicide", "Antibiotic",
                                   "Drought_MP", "Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_MP", 
                                   "Drought_Herbicide", "Antibiotic_Drought", "Antibiotic_Herbicide",
                                   "Drought_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_MP", 
                                   "Antibiotic_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide", 
                                   "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide_MP"))

df_plot$Treatment <- factor(df_plot$Treatment, levels = levels(treatment_order))


ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = Treatment, y = Distance_to_Control)) + 
  geom_point(color = "black", size = 3) + 
  ylab("Mean Bray-Curtis distance to Control") + 
  xlab("Treatment") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))


### building a full 172x172 bray-curtis distance matrix where every experimental unit is compared to every other experimental unit
# this is a cleaner and more flexible approach than pre-averaging the distances, and I can compute means with standard errors or confidence intervals for each Control-treatment (or treatment-treatment) pair
dist_full <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_mse1.filtered3, method = "bray")
dist_full_mat <- as.matrix(dist_full)

Stress <- smd$Stress_ID

# compute mean distance (and spread) from control to each treatment 
control_label <- "Control"  
treats          <- unique(Stress)
other_treats    <- treats[treats != control_label]

# Storage
res <- data.frame(
  Treatment = character(),
  Distance_to_Control = numeric(),
  SE = numeric(),
  n_pairs = integer(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (trt in other_treats) {
  # Indices of samples in Control
  s_ctrl  <- which(Stress == control_label)
  # Indices of samples in treatment `trt`
  s_trt   <- which(Stress == trt)
  
  # All Control–Treatment distances (each Control rep vs each trt rep)
  d_ctl_trt <- dist_full_mat[s_ctrl, s_trt]
  
  # Mean and SE
  m <- mean(d_ctl_trt)
  se <- sd(d_ctl_trt) / sqrt(length(d_ctl_trt))
  n_pairs <- length(d_ctl_trt)
  
  res <- rbind(res, data.frame(
    Treatment = trt,
    Distance_to_Control = m,
    SE = se,
    n_pairs = n_pairs, 
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

# now add a column for the distance between each rep and the control 
res$dist_to_mean_reps <- vector("list", nrow(res))

for (i in 1:nrow(res)) {
  trt <- res$Treatment[i]
  s_ctrl <- which(Stress == control_label)
  s_trt <- which(Stress == trt)
  
  mean_dist_per_trt_rep <- apply(dist_full_mat[s_trt, s_ctrl, drop = FALSE], 1, mean) - res$Distance_to_Control[i]
  res$dist_to_mean_reps[[i]] <- mean_dist_per_trt_rep
}

# Optional: sort by distance
#res <- res[order(res$Distance_to_Control, decreasing = TRUE), ]


# sort x axis 
treatment_order <- factor(c("MP", "Drought", "Herbicide", "Antibiotic",
                          "Drought_MP", "Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_MP",

                          "Drought_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_MP", 
                          "Antibiotic_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide", 
                          "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide_MP"), 
                         levels = c("MP", "Drought", "Herbicide", "Antibiotic",
                                   "Drought_MP", "Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_MP", 
                                   "Drought_Herbicide", "Antibiotic_Drought", "Antibiotic_Herbicide",
                                   "Drought_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_MP", 
                                   "Antibiotic_Herbicide_MP", "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide", 
                                   "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide_MP"))

res$Treatment <- factor(res$Treatment, levels = levels(treatment_order))

# plot with variation around the mean
```

```{r}
# creating the same distance matrix above, but with Jensen-Shannon Distance/Divergence) 
# this is a similarity metric between two probability distributions (like microbiome compositions)
# so 0 = identical communities; 1 = completely different 

# JSD emphasizes compositional differences (ignores absolute abundance), while Bray-Curtis weights by total abundance differences 
# JSD might be better since I rarefied/preprocessed to equal depth 
# results should be similar between JSD and Bray-Curtis, but maybe less extreme values with JSD 

dist_jsd <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_mse1.filtered3, "jsd") 
dist_jsd_matrix <- as.matrix(dist_jsd)

  s_trt   <- which(Stress == trt)

  d_ctl_trt_jsd <- dist_jsd_matrix[s_ctrl, s_trt]
  
  # Mean and SE
  m <- mean(d_ctl_trt_jsd)
  se <- sd(d_ctl_trt_jsd) / sqrt(length(d_ctl_trt_jsd))
  n_pairs <- length(d_ctl_trt_jsd)
  
  res_jsd <- rbind(res_jsd, data.frame(
    Treatment = trt,
    Distance_to_Control_jsd = m,
    SE = se,
    n_pairs = n_pairs, 
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

# now add a column for the distance between each rep and the control
```

```{r}
#### 3-stress combo subsets 
focal_3stress <- "Drought_Herbicide_MP" 

# define the 1-stress and 2-stress combos that are subsets of the focal 3-stress 
sub_stress_levels <- c(
  "Control", 
  "Drought", 
  "Herbicide", 
  "MP", 
  "Drought_Herbicide", 
  "Drought_MP", 
  "Herbicide_MP",
  "Antibiotic_Drought_Herbicide_MP"
)

# samples belonging to the focal 3-stress group 
samples_3stress <- smd$ID[smd$Stress_ID == focal_3stress]
samples_subset <- smd$ID[smd$Stress_ID %in% sub_stress_levels]

# extract distances from subset to 3-stress 
# subset from big distance matrix so sample names match up 
dis_ids <- rownames(dist_full_mat)
samples_3stress <- dis_ids[dis_ids %in% smd$ID[smd$Stress_ID == focal_3stress]]
samples_subset <- dis_ids[dis_ids %in% smd$ID[smd$Stress_ID %in% sub_stress_levels]]

samples_all <- unique(c(samples_subset, samples_3stress))   
D_sub <- dist_full_mat[samples_all, samples_all]

# prepare to plot

#  Identify which rows of D_sub are 1‑/2‑stress vs 3‑stress
is_3stress <- rownames(D_sub) %in% samples_3stress
is_other   <- !is_3stress

pairwise_df <- NULL
# calculate the pairwise distance between two groups and THEN average them for plotting (this allows for SE)
for (stress in sub_stress_levels) {
  # Get IDs in this stress level (1‑ or 2‑stress)
  ids_in_stress <- smd %>%
    filter(Stress_ID == stress, ID %in% rownames(D_sub)) %>%
    pull(ID)

  if (length(ids_in_stress) == 0) next

  # Get all 3‑stress IDs that appear in D_sub
  ids_3stress <- sample_names(physeq_mse1.filtered3)[
    sample_names(physeq_mse1.filtered3) %in% rownames(D_sub)
  ][is_3stress]

  # Extract all pairwise distances between stress and 3‑stress
  for (id_s in ids_in_stress) {
    for (id_3 in ids_3stress) {
      pairwise_df <- rbind(pairwise_df, data.frame(
        Stress_ID = stress,
        from = id_s,
        to = id_3,
        distance = D_sub[id_s, id_3]
      ))
    }
  }
}

pairwise_df$Stress_ID <- factor(pairwise_df$Stress_ID, levels = sub_stress_levels)

# 3. Summarize: mean pairwise distance + SE per stress level
pairwise_summ <- pairwise_df %>%
  group_by(Stress_ID) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_dist = mean(distance, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(distance, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 4. Point + SE plot (same graphic style, different distance metric)
Dr_Hb_MP_mean_BC_distance <- ggplot(pairwise_summ, aes(x = Stress_ID, y = mean_dist)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, colour = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean_dist - se, ymax = mean_dist + se),
    width = 0.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  labs(x = "Component Stress Treatments",
    y = "Mean Bray-Curtis pairwise distance to D + H + MP") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))


ggsave("~/Desktop/FDA_Lab/Experiment1/plots/Dr_Hb_MP_mean_BC_distance.png", Dr_Hb_MP_mean_BC_distance)

# heatmap 
# group first by treatment
meta_group <- smd %>%
  filter(ID %in% samples_all) %>%
  select(ID, Stress_ID) %>%
  mutate(ID = as.character(ID))

# Put it in the same order as D_sub
meta_group <- meta_group[match(rownames(D_sub), meta_group$ID), ]

# List of stress levels to compare
stress_levels <- unique(meta_group$Stress_ID)

# convert to distance matrix for heatmap plotting 
bg_mat <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(stress_levels), ncol = length(stress_levels))
rownames(bg_mat) <- colnames(bg_mat) <- stress_levels

for (i in seq_along(stress_levels)) {
  for (j in seq_along(stress_levels)) {
    grp_i <- meta_group$ID[meta_group$Stress_ID == stress_levels[i]]
    grp_j <- meta_group$ID[meta_group$Stress_ID == stress_levels[j]]

    dists_ij <- sapply(grp_i, function(x) sapply(grp_j, function(y) D_sub[x, y]))
    bg_mat[i, j] <- mean(dists_ij, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}


pheatmap(bg_mat, 
         main = "Mean Bray-Curtis Distances",
         fontsize_row = 9, fontsize_col = 9, 
         filename = "~/Desktop/FDA_Lab/Experiment1/plots/dr_hb_mp_mean_bd_distance_heatmap.png")
```

```{r}
# remember that res is the df that has the mean distance to control from each treatment  
res

# subset to only include the single stresses 
res_single <- res[res$Treatment %in% c("Drought", "MP", "Herbicide", "Antibiotic"), ]

# compute angle for each treatment (evenly spaced)
n <- nrow(res_single)
res_single$angle <- seq(0, 2*pi, length.out = n + 1)[- (n + 1)]

# convert to Cartesian coordinates for the arrow endpoints 
res_single <- res_single %>% 
  mutate(
    x = Distance_to_Control * cos(angle), 
    y = Distance_to_Control * sin(angle), 
    x_se_lo = (Distance_to_Control - SE) * cos(angle), 
    x_se_hi = (Distance_to_Control + SE) * cos(angle), 
    y_se_lo = (Distance_to_Control - SE) * sin(angle), 
    y_se_hi = (Distance_to_Control + SE) * sin(angle)
  )

ggplot() + 
  # control at (0, 0) as a circle 
  geom_point(
    aes(x = 0, y = 0), 
    size = 4, color = "black", fill = "white", shape = 21) + 
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "Control", vjust = -1) + 
  # arrows from Control to each treatment 
  geom_segment(
    data = res_single, 
    aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = x, yend = y), 
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), 
    color = "black", 
    size = 1) + 
  # treatment balls at the end of arrow ends 
  geom_point(
    data = res_single, 
    aes(x = x, y =y), 
    size = 4, color = "black", fill = "skyblue", shape = 21) + 
  geom_text(
    data = res_single, 
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = Treatment), 
    hjust = 1.5, vjust = -0.5, size = 4) 


# since the distances between single stress treatments and control are very close to each other, I'm going to move the angles so the treatments are closer together and easier to compare 

res_single_angle <- res_single %>% 
  mutate( 
    #map the treatments to a smaller angular window: 45º to 315 º
    angle_raw = seq(45, -45, length.out = n()), 
    #convert degrees to radians 
    angle = angle_raw * pi / 180,
    # cartesian coordinates 
    x = Distance_to_Control * cos(angle), 
    y = Distance_to_Control * sin(angle), 
    x_se_lo = (Distance_to_Control - SE) * cos(angle), 
    x_se_hi = (Distance_to_Control + SE) * cos(angle), 
    y_se_lo = (Distance_to_Control - SE) * sin(angle), 
    y_se_hi = (Distance_to_Control + SE) * sin(angle)
    )

 radial_control_to_single_stress <- ggplot() + 
  # control at (0, 0) as a circle 
  geom_point(
    aes(x = 0, y = 0), 
    size = 4, color = "black", fill = "#e6194B", shape = 21) + 
  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "Control", vjust = -2) + 
  # arrows from Control to each treatment 
  geom_segment(
    data = res_single_angle, 
    aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = x, yend = y), 
    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), 
    color = "black", 
    size = 1) + 
  # treatment balls at the end of arrow ends 
  geom_point(
    data = res_single_angle, 
    aes(x = x, y = y, fill = Treatment), 
    size = 6, color = "black", shape = 21) + 
   scale_fill_manual(values = c( 
       "Drought" = "#ffe119",
       "MP" = "#3cb44b", 
      "Herbicide" = "#4363d8", 
      "Antibiotic" = "#f58231"))
 #+
#  geom_text(
#    data = res_single_angle, 
#    aes(x = x, y = y, label = Treatment), 
#    hjust = 1.5, vjust = -0.5, size = 4)

ggsave("~/Desktop/FDA_Lab/Experiment1/plots/radial_control_to_single_stress.svg", radial_control_to_single_stress, width = 5, height = 6)


# lollipop plot 
lollipop_distace_to_control <- ggplot(res_single, aes(x = Distance_to_Control, y = reorder(Treatment, Distance_to_Control))) + # sort by distances
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = Distance_to_Control, y = reorder(Treatment, Distance_to_Control), yend = reorder(Treatment, Distance_to_Control)), color = "gray50", size = 1) + 
  geom_point(aes(fill = Treatment), size = 6, color = "gray50", shape = 21) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("MP" = "#3cb44b", "Drought" = "#ffe119", "Herbicide" = "#4363d8", "Antibiotic" = "#f58231")) + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.30, 0.36)) +

c(length(d_DMP_MP), head(d_DMP_MP))

mean(d_DMP_MP)
sd(d_DMP_MP)

mean(d_DMP_D)
sd(d_DMP_D)

drought_mp_distances <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("MP",
                 "Drought"),

                  sd(d_DMP_D,  na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(length(d_DMP_D)))
)

n <- nrow(drought_mp_distances)


drought_mp_distance_angle <- drought_mp_distances %>% 
  mutate( 
    #map the treatments to a smaller angular window: 45º to 315º
    angle_raw = seq(30, -30, length.out = n), 
    #convert degrees to radians 
    angle = angle_raw * pi / 180,
    # cartesian coordinates 
    x = mean_dist * cos(angle), 
    y = mean_dist * sin(angle), 
    x_se_lo = (mean_dist - SE) * cos(angle), 
    x_se_hi = (mean_dist + SE) * cos(angle), 
    y_se_lo = (mean_dist - SE) * sin(angle), 
    y_se_hi = (mean_dist + SE) * sin(angle)
    )

radial_drought_mp <- ggplot() + 
  # control at (0, 0) as a circle

  annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "Drought + MP", vjust = -2.5, hjust = -0.15) + 
  # arrows from Drought + MP to each single stress treatment 
  geom_segment(

    arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm")), 
    color = "black", 
    size = 1) +

  geom_point(

   scale_fill_manual(values = c( 
       "Drought" = "#ffe119",
       "MP" = "#3cb44b"))
```

```{r}
### Network graph  
# each stress treatment = nodes, and edges connect higher-order connections 
# edge width = distance 

library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(ggplot2)

two_stress   <- read_excel("~/Desktop/FDA_Lab/Experiment1/data/MSE1_BrayCurtisDistances.xlsx", sheet = "Two_Stress")
three_stress <- read_excel("~/Desktop/FDA_Lab/Experiment1/data/MSE1_BrayCurtisDistances.xlsx", sheet = "Three_Stress")
four_stress   <- read_excel("~/Desktop/FDA_Lab/Experiment1/data/MSE1_BrayCurtisDistances.xlsx", sheet = "Four_Stress")

make_edges <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = starts_with("Distance_to_"),
      names_to = "To",
      values_to = "Distance"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Distance)) %>%
    mutate(
      Distance = as.numeric(Distance),
      From = sub("^Distance_to_", "", To),
      To = Treatment
    ) %>%
    select(From, To, Distance)
}

edges <- bind_rows(
  make_edges(two_stress),
  make_edges(three_stress),
  make_edges(four_stress)
)

nodes <- tibble(name = unique(c(edges$From, edges$To))) %>%
  mutate(
    level = stringr::str_count(name, "_") + 1
  )

g <- graph_from_data_frame(edges, vertices = nodes, directed = FALSE)

ggraph(g, layout = "sugiyama") +
  geom_edge_link(aes(width = Distance, color = Distance), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_node_point(aes(fill = factor(level)), shape = 21, size = 5, color = "gray30") +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name), repel = TRUE, size = 3) +
  scale_edge_width(range = c(0.4, 2.2)) +
  #scale_edge_color_viridis_c() +
  theme_void() +
  labs(fill = "Stress order", edge_color = "Bray-Curtis")
```
